measurements.tradeoff: One-parameter self tail calls without extra locals avoid frame/root reconstruction. Self-tail invocation instruction counts fall by 4.8–6.4%; mutual tail calls and extra-local self tail calls add 0.48% and 0.82%, respectively. Non-tail workloads retain their instruction counts. measurements.tradeoff: Alternating fresh hosted constructions improve 3.7% (11.91 to 11.47 ms); the sequential pair improves 2.2%. Hosted line-comment, mixed-length name and wide-integer loads improve 24.3%, 16.1% and 7.6%; short integer/many-function and mixed-whitespace loads slow by about 4%. Fresh construction continues to instantiate an independent bootstrap and parse the complete readable engine source. Bounded word scanning speeds atoms, uniform indentation and ordinary line comments; each atom/whitespace run switches once to its byte tail after a possible boundary. No prepared state or compilation cache is introduced. Construction and guest loading are measured separately, with mixed whitespace included as a control.

measurements.label: Same-memory copy and guest growth bookkeeping
measurements.timingNote: Standalone hosted audit after the complete test suite. Paired invocation samples run sequentially with no compilation, test or audit overlap; all twenty-seven workloads use identical inputs. Full spec stress inputs remain unchanged. measurements.tradeoff: Same-memory copy avoids reselecting its source/destination descriptor; growth by zero retains its validated size immediately. Positive growth retains backing checks and zeroing, moves following bytes only when present, and visits only later memory descriptors. All paired workload inputs and full spec stress inputs are unchanged. Alternating hosted copy loops improve 10.6% with 5.06% fewer instructions; zero-growth loops improve 3.9% with 4.34% fewer instructions. Fill/failure/memory/ordinary-call controls retain their counts and stay roughly flat in timing. Sixteen-page last-memory growth improves 5.3–10.4% with about 3.3% fewer instructions; growth relocating a following memory has mixed timings and about 1% fewer instructions.

invocationBenchmarkAlternating.method: Alternating before/after hosted invocations in one process, both engines warmed, no concurrent compilation/tests/audits.

positiveGrowthBenchmark.method: Alternating hosted invocations growing sixteen pages in a fresh guest each repeat; interpreter construction, guest loading and result checks excluded. Counts use a separate instrumented native parent with no child markers.

measurements.label: Sequential scalar validation, scalar memory dispatch and public host invocation improvements

stages.name: Scalar validation
stages.tradeoff: Fixed scalar signatures use the existing packed effect metadata; validation-pop/value retain stack-floor, polymorphic unreachable, type and capacity checks.

stages.name: Scalar memory dispatch
stages.tradeoff: Dedicated scalar operand/result handling uses unchanged resource-apply/address helpers and selects memory on every operation. SIMD/bulk and generic resource paths remain unchanged.

stages.name: Hybrid opcode route metadata
stages.tradeoff: Dense scalar/control route bytes and packed extended routes fit the existing reserved space, but sequential timings regress about 1–3% for scalar and about 5% for SIMD. Experiment reverted before final validation.

stages.name: Host invocation

benchmark.guest:
(module
  (func (export "scalar") (param i32 i32) (result i32) local.get 0 local.get 1 i32.add)
  (func (export "float") (param f64) (result f64) local.get 0)
  (func (export "vector") (param v128) (result v128) local.get 0)
  (func (export "many") (param i32 i64 f64 v128) (result i32 i64 f64 v128)
    local.get 0 local.get 1 local.get 2 local.get 3))

stages.tradeoff: Reuse each invocation’s freshly resolved index, omit unused result signature queries, and read shared argument-high base and scalar result type once. No persistent signature, engine or checkpoint cache.

measurements.timingNote: Stages measured sequentially. Host comparison alternates warmed old/new frontends on identical final engines with seven samples and 1,000 public calls per sample; its old frontend differs only in absolute default asset URLs. Timing loops exclude construction and verification. No compilation/tests/audits overlap timed benchmarks. Full suite and standalone audits run sequentially; stress inputs and frozen coverage unchanged. No CI performance thresholds.

measurements.label: Trimmed scalar memory access and scalar floating-point dispatch

stages.name: Earlier scalar memory dispatch
stages.tradeoff: Moved the existing scalar memory handler immediately after integer dispatch. Alternating memory gain was less than 1%, while call/control workloads regressed. Reverted before stage two.

stages.name: Trim scalar memory selection and helpers
stages.tradeoff: Select canonical memory on every access but refresh only pages/base/address type. Shared scalar width and checked load/store helpers bypass unrelated resource/SIMD probes; stores return immediately. Growth/bulk/SIMD continue selecting complete descriptors.

stages.name: Scalar floating-point dispatch
stages.tradeoff: Fixed unary/binary float signatures use compact scalar operand slots and replace the consumed left slot, with zero high bits. The unchanged float-apply implementation retains NaN/overflow checks, exact result bits, and guest fuel.

benchmarkInputs.floatArithmetic: f32.add/eq and f64.div/sqrt in a 5,000-iteration loop
benchmarkInputs.floatConversions: f64.convert_i64_u/i64.trunc_f64_s and i32.trunc_sat_f32_s in a 5,000-iteration loop

measurements.timingNote: Candidates evaluated in order. Twenty-nine sequential workloads use 5,000 iterations and five samples; eight hosted controls use seven alternating samples on warmed old/new engines. Guest correctness checks remain in benchmark scripts. No compilation/tests/audits overlap timed benchmarks. Complete suite and standalone audits run sequentially. Full spec stress inputs, frozen coverage and default optimized build are unchanged; no CI timing thresholds or persistent engine/signature caches.

measurements.label: Balanced floating opcode tree, precomputed access width and fresh hosted metadata snapshots

stages.name: Balanced floating helper dispatch
stages.tradeoff: Generate a balanced opcode tree with exact-match leaves of at most three entries. NaN/overflow guards, operand/result conversions and unsupported-opcode zero fallback remain unchanged.

stages.name: Precomputed memory access width
stages.tradeoff: Store natural width at offset 28 of the existing 32-byte memarg record. Text and decoded binary share parsing; runtime scalar checks read the field, independent of alignment hints. No arena growth or changed instruction record sizes.

measurements.buildModeFix: Compare the serialized flags when make reads the Makefile, and force every derived stage on a mode/configuration change. This fixes stale debug artifacts after rapid release switches on coarse-timestamp make versions. No tool rebuild occurs when flags are unchanged.
measurements.tradeoffs: Compact source improves paired construction 19%; most loader/execution controls are close, with 4-6% memory/vector execution gains. Matched complete audit improves 10%, including 17% lower construction time. Ordinary formatted optimized WAT regresses construction 24% and is not used. Accidental stale-debug artifacts were diagnosed, excluded from release performance claims, and release-only verification was rerun after the build fix. No compiled bootstrap module reuse or hosted state cache.

measurements.label: Reuse caller-owned compiled bootstrap modules

pairedStandaloneAudit.method: Same release binary and optimized interpreter WAT. Baseline reads/instantiates bootstrap bytes per engine; after compiles once per suite and instantiates fresh state. One-time preparation is included in total/other. Runs are sequential on the same machine.

measurements.tradeoffs: Explicit caller-owned WebAssembly.Module only. No global path cache or interpreter snapshot. Fresh native instance, hosted WAT parse/load, guest state and frontend adapters per factory call. Avoids repeated file IO and byte-based instantiation; Node can already cache compiled byte input, so the measured saving is not attributed solely to compilation. The paired audit saves 10.64s of construction, offset by 5.86s slower loading; execution is flat. Overall gain is about 4%, and phase changes may include scheduling/GC effects.

measurements.label: Compare Binaryen speed and size presets with explicit metadata stripping

validation.context: Full suite verified selected release runtime first. Seven private probe compiler invocations and phase diagnostic were then aligned from O4 to Oz and reverified with all 19 affected tests; no runtime code changed.

measurements.method: All candidates derive from identical raw release bytes; size presets include convergence and both strips. Alternate candidate order in construction and execution samples. Complete standalone audits run sequentially Os, Oz, O4 on the same machine. The duplicated O4 control is byte-identical yet has some large execution timing differences; do not treat those noisy individual ratios as reliable speedups. Full audits retain unchanged frozen stress inputs.
measurements.stripping: Both individual strip-debug and combined strip-debug/strip-producers leave current O4 wasm and WAT byte-for-byte unchanged. No debug/producers sections are present. Keep explicit stripping in release configuration only.
measurements.passInspection: Binaryen 133 rejects --print-passes. make inspect-opt uses BINARYEN_PASS_DEBUG=1, the mechanism used by installed upstream unit tests, with stable ordered names printed in CI and full diagnostics in build/opt-passes.log. A traced Oz build is byte-identical to its untraced build.

selectionReconsidered.reason: Prefer interpreter execution speed and overall speed/size balance. Oz saves 5.5% wasm and 7.9% WAT but costs about 4.6% execution and 0.5% total in the standalone comparison. Normal native callers do not incur hosted interpreter construction. Strips, feature validation and pass-order diagnostics remain retained.

measurements.label: Run the complete test matrix through separate WAT and WASM targets
measurements.method: Run make check then make check-wasm sequentially on the same unchanged release artifacts. Shared cases select only their target runtime; previously parameterized pairs are split across CI targets, so each run has fewer registered tests. Dedicated self-host/default-API and mixed-owner tests stay explicit. One new parent-fuel behavior test verifies the selected factory executes at the requested runtime depth. Reports use distinct paths. Production API and runner defaults remain unchanged.

measurements.label: Fuse adjacent local/local integer binary operations
measurements.method: Identical frontend and O4 convergence flags; before/after binary and optimized WAT snapshots. Nine alternating fresh-construction rounds of ten factories. Execution uses three independent instances per variant/runtime/case, three 1000-iteration warmups, five alternating 5000-iteration samples; use median of instance medians. No tests or audits overlap benchmarks. Complete check-wat then check-wasm retain the frozen stress inputs. Before suite timing is historical, not a paired suite claim.
measurements.tradeoffs: Matching loops improve about 29-31% native and 36% hosted. Construction is flat. Unrelated controls mostly vary 1-3%, with a 3.6% native memory slowdown in this sample set. Binary grows 68 bytes and compact WAT 501 bytes. Keep exact fuel and intermediate capacity by falling back to ordinary dispatch; do not fuse division/remainder or vector/float operations. Reuse existing opcode marker and record format, without guest compilation or a new instruction representation. Controlled complete hosted audit improves 1.34% overall (133093.9665 to 131305.422083 ms), including 1.05s lower execution. Both pass all commands; the earlier slower suite compared with historical timing is not attributed to the patch.

pairedStandaloneAudit.method: Same current frontend and runner, unchanged O4 flags and frozen inventory. Before source/binary snapshot followed by current source/binary in sequential complete audits; no tests or benchmarks overlap. Explicit source URLs and import paths are the only scratch runner changes.

measurements.label: Native SIMD for wrapping integer arithmetic, equality and all-true reductions
measurements.method: Before local-fusion snapshot and after SIMD source/binary use identical frontend. Nine alternating construction rounds of ten factories; execution has three independent instances per variant/runtime/case, three 1000-iteration warmups and five alternating 5000-iteration samples, median of instance medians. Workloads include result equality/all-true checks, so gains in untouched math/memory families reflect faster checks rather than changes to those operations. No tests/audits overlap timed benchmarks. Full targets run sequentially. Suite baselines are historical and no controlled full-suite speedup is claimed.
measurements.tradeoffs: Eighteen exact integer primitives use native SIMD internally: eight wrapping add/sub/mul, six eq/ne, four all_true reductions. Other families remain scalar. Checked vector workloads improve 14-25% native and 22-34% hosted; scalar controls are roughly flat. Construction improves 2% in this sample set. WASM shrinks 1035 bytes and WAT 7669 bytes. Host bootstrap now requires SIMD; flags and diagnostic probe compilers enable it explicitly. No alternate runtime branch, guest compiler, new ABI or loss of self-hosting. Native WAT SIMD opcodes are interpreted at hosted levels and terminate at the native bootstrap.

measurements.label: Native SIMD for ordered comparisons, shifts, saturation, narrowing and bitmasks
measurements.method: Immutable preceding SIMD baseline and selected release use the same frontend. Nine alternating construction rounds of ten fresh factories. Execution uses three independent instances per variant/runtime/case, three 1000-iteration warmups, and five alternating 1000-iteration samples; median of instance medians. Checked workload groups cover all 56 new primitives using a separate BigInt lane model; result checks and scalar loop overhead remain in measured execution. No tests/audits overlap timed benchmarks. Full WAT then WASM targets run sequentially. A follow-up matched full-spec pair per runtime uses the same current frontend and runner with immutable preceding/current binary and WAT, before then after, without overlapping work. Hosted total improves 2.34%; native total increases 1.21%, mostly harness time, with native execution increasing 0.47%.
measurements.tradeoffs: Replace 56 scalar lane loops: 28 ordered comparisons, 12 shifts, eight saturating add/subtract operations, four narrow conversions and four bitmasks. Exact vector instructions keep the existing two-i64 ABI and dispatch. Targeted 8/16/32-bit groups improve 3-14% natively and 5-23% hosted; 64-bit groups improve around 2%. Bitmask workload improves 7% native and 14% hosted. Construction improves 4.3%. WASM shrinks 3948 bytes and optimized WAT 28900 bytes. Native scalar controls vary +1-3% while hosted controls improve 2-4%. Matched full hosted audit improves 2.34%; native audit is 1.21% slower, mostly harness variation. No guest compilation, cached state or extra host requirement beyond already-enabled SIMD.

measurements.label: Bulk normalized GC array filling and zeroed default constructors
measurements.method: Immutable preceding SIMD baseline and selected release use identical frontend. Fifteen alternating construction rounds of ten fresh factories, guest checks outside timing. Execution: three independent instances per variant/runtime/case, three warmups of 16 iterations and five alternating 64-iteration samples, median of instance medians. Module reload outside every timed sample resets the fixed object arena so constructor tests cannot exhaust it; no guest state is cached. Values/lengths and both vector halves are checked inside measured loops. No audits or tests overlap timed benchmarks. Full WAT then WASM targets run sequentially; full timings are historical comparisons, not a paired full-suite speedup claim.
measurements.tradeoffs: Normalize the first raw slot via gc-store, then copy a bounded initialized prefix geometrically. array.new and array.fill use the helper; array.new_default retains the allocator zeroing without redundant element stores; array.new_fixed preserves distinct reverse-pop order. Large 4096-element cases improve 68-91% native and 95-97% hosted; 512-reference fill improves 67%/77%. Small native fill/new cases can regress around 9-12%, at roughly 16-19 microseconds for 64 checked iterations. Fresh hosted construction is 0.6% slower; WASM grows 83 bytes and WAT 564 bytes. Complete test time remains roughly flat in historical comparisons. No new arena, object layout, guest compilation or prepared interpreter state.
